paper_role: E6b interaction-level bridge with two independent published systems; supports response-asymmetry-to-interaction-timing change but not theoretical deadline costs

source.citation: Burgess MD et al. 2018. Tritrophic phenological match-mismatch in space and time. Nature Ecology & Evolution 2:970-975.
source.source_note: Published bivariate MCMCglmm analysis of UK oak-caterpillar-bird phenology; bird first-egg dates came from the BTO Nest Record Scheme and are not redistributed here.

estimand.definition: major-axis slope of higher-trophic-level phenology on lower-trophic-level phenology across years
estimand.interpretation: slope < 1 means the consumer shifts less among years than the resource, generating temporal variation in relative timing

interaction_pairs.pair: peak caterpillar biomass -> blue tit first egg date
peak caterpillar biomass -> great tit first egg date
peak caterpillar biomass -> pied flycatcher first egg date

licensed_interpretation: In three real bird-caterpillar interactions, consumer phenology tracks year-to-year resource phenology incompletely; the pairwise response disparity converts earlier resource years into larger timing mismatch. This is interaction-level evidence for response-asymmetry-to-mismatch, not a direct estimate of information-deadline difference.
not_licensed: the theoretical delay-cost difference D2-D1 has been measured
the q1 < q <= q2 asynchronous information-use window has been observed
information distance is the causal mechanism for the pairwise tracking deficits
pied flycatchers are more mismatched because of migration distance alone
the published Burgess pattern is a new PAYOFF-B discovery

additional_source.citation: Samplonius JM et al. 2018. Phenological sensitivity to climate change is higher in resident than in migrant bird populations among European cavity breeders. Global Change Biology 24:3780-3790.
additional_source.design: 10 European nest-box schemes, 1991-2015, each with at least one resident tit and one migratory flycatcher population
additional_source.interaction_context: resident tits and migratory flycatchers overlap in nest-site competition and breeding ecology
additional_source.licensed_interpretation: Resident and migratory cavity breeders sharing breeding ecology have different temperature sensitivities, and those differences have already widened their phenological interval through time.
not_licensed: statistical climate windows are decision deadlines
migration strategy alone causally explains the temperature-sensitivity difference
the theoretical D2-D1 parameter has been measured
the q1<q<=q2 information-use window has been observed

bridge_synthesis.burgess_2018: consumer-resource pair response asymmetry -> mismatch in early springs
bridge_synthesis.samplonius_2018: resident-migrant competitor response asymmetry -> widening laying-date interval
bridge_synthesis.combined: Two independent interaction contexts show that unequal phenological responsiveness among interacting partners changes their relative timing.
bridge_synthesis.mechanism_boundary: Neither study identifies waiting cost D nor information-use thresholds q1/q2.
